chapters.title: Chapter 5130: Greed! II
paragraphs: The seas of Infinity dispersed around him, and the skies of a grand floating island opened into his perception.

The light filtered through something that wasn’t atmosphere, golden currents of Observable Force braiding through the open sky in slow rivers that curved around the island’s edges without ever touching them. Below, the island stretched wide and terraced, its pale stone surface veined with gold that pulsed in patient rhythms, its towers rising at the corners with their blinking arrays of polished lenses.
Information poured into him from every direction.
The weavings of Infinity carried the signatures of every being present, the configurations of every structure, the residue of every experiment that had been conducted on this island.
Observable Force layered its own data over the top. It was abundant, the kind of abundance that would have drowned a lesser perception in static, and he let all of it flow freely across his mind!
It passed in less than an instant.
Even in its density, even in the sheer volume of what was being given to him, he received it and read it and filed it in a span shorter than an instant.
|Domain Entry: Unnamed Research Archipelago, THE Wyld.|
|Entity Count: Seven Primordial Architects confirmed present on the primary island. Six distant islands hold additional entities. Full classification pending.|
The information settled into place, and his eyes shone brightly as he looked ahead.
Many eyes looked back.

The silence that fell was awkward! Nobody moved and nobody spoke. The apparatus continued its quiet hum. The golden table at the center continued to receive its rivers of Infinity. The corpse on that table continued its mechanical breathing.
The island spread out beneath him in full view now.

Corpses lay across multiple tables, each one a Primordial Architect in some stage of dissection or modification. Protruding fungi grew from their exposed organs. Pale tendrils wound through their rib cages. Some of the bodies twitched faintly with residual life. Others were clearly past the point of any return. Each table was its own quiet experiment, each subject a record of some attempt that had either succeeded along a narrow axis or failed in an instructive manner.
At the center, a single table commanded the rest.

The corpse lying on it radiated something the others didn’t. Terrifying power rolled off its fungus-laced body in slow waves. Potent Infinity pulsed through the rivers being fed into it, the flow rates higher than anything feeding the other tables.
The Primordial Architects of this research party had clustered near it.
Noah focused on the ones carrying the most power.
|Entity Detected: Octavius Kraethos, Designer of THE Primordial Mycelia.|
|Status: Surprised but composed.|
|Current Scale: THE Proterozoic Scale - Calymmian Tier(Seems fake, power does not match).|
|Threat Level: Significant? Unknown|
|Entity Detected: Valeria Morne, Research Peer.|
|Status: Alert and guarded.|
|Current Scale: THE Proterozoic Scale - Calymmian Tier.|
|Threat Level: Less significant.|
His gaze settled on Octavius.
So this was the one who had created the Primordial Mycelia. The scholar who had forged the fungus of Unity that Erwin had taken!
The entity whose research had rippled outward through so many downstream consequences that even Emotive’s claiming of Chaos traced back to his table!
What a wonder of causality.
All of that had been conceived on a floating island like this one, probably on this exact island, under the steady patient hands of the being now staring back at him.
Looking at Octavius, and at a few of the others clustered near him, brought a unique sensation into his perception.
Seas of Infinity moved within their bodies.

Seas! The concentration held by each of these engineered Primordial Architects exceeded anything he had encountered in any Primordial Architect before, and the seas were stable in a way that made no immediate sense. They should have been drowning. They should have been losing themselves to THE Gamaidian, the madness that Infinity inflicted on beings who couldn’t withstand its pressure.
Instead, the seas held themselves in orderly shorelines inside each of them, kept that way by engineering that had been written into their existential foundations.
The so called amplification of Ego.

Was this what Emotive had been describing? Emotions inflated to such intensity that they could stand against the natural superiority of Infinity, push back against its madness, create a stable foundation on which the sea could rest without spilling over?
The curiosity that bloomed inside him was sharp!

He wanted to gauge their power. He wanted to open their bodies and see exactly what made them tick. The engineering was right there in front of him, walking and speaking and preparing to resist him, and all he had to do was get his hands around one of them to begin the study!
All of this passed through him in a span that measured below a nanosecond.
Below him, the Primordial Architects had already gathered closer to their leader.

Octavius looked at him and at Naldine with eyes that couldn’t quite believe what they were seeing. A deep smile bloomed across his face, slow and scholarly and unsettling in its warmth. His pale gold eyes held focused intensity.
"This... is absolutely incredible."
His voice carried the cadence of a master who had just received an unexpected gift.

"A lot might have truly underestimated you, Infinity-bearer. I saw you when you were broadcasting your thrashing of Beowulf, and the recording was instructive, genuinely instructive, but seeing you in person is something else entirely. It’s a treat. Honestly, a treat!"
He took a small step forward, his hands clasped lightly behind his back.

"Listen. I have many internal laboratories ready for use, quite nearby, well prepared and well equipped. If you’d be willing to cooperate with the process, I can lay you down on a table and open you up just to study your Infinity a little bit. Nothing too invasive. I just don’t want things to get messy and loud and have any others come by. The integrity of the research depends on quiet, you understand."
Noah opened his mouth to tell Octavius that he didn’t have to worry about any interruptions.
Emotive’s voice beat him to it.
"Haha!"
Her voice echoed out across the floating island with all the singsong mania she had been holding back in the forest.
"Soon-to-be-corpse, you don’t have to worry about that! I! Have! Sealed! Everything!"
Yes.

The moment they had arrived, both Emotive and Naldine had exerted power in their own unique ways, each of them operating on their own initiative without needing him to direct them. He had felt the twin workings settle into place alongside his arrival. He hadn’t needed to make a single move of his own to lock this region down.
|Emotional Blockade has been established. Authority: THE Living Emotive.|

|All information capable of traveling on weavings of emotion and chaos has been severed within the surrounding region of approximately one gigaparsec. Complete existential silence has been declared. An Ediacaran Tier entity would require several minutes to overcome this blockade.|
|THE Hadean Barrier of Infinity has been enacted. Authority: Naldine Manthon.|

|All weavings of information expressed through Infinity have been prevented from entering or exiting the surrounding region of approximately ten gigaparsecs. No signal, plea, or distress weaving will reach any outside party.|
The notifications settled into the space between his thoughts.

He looked at the unique Primordial Architects glowing with their seas of Infinity, their engineered stability holding their frames against pressures that should have collapsed them. Even he couldn’t say for certain whether these would be decent enemies or whether a few of them would actually give him trouble.
The seas inside them were real. The engineering was grand. These were not the ordinary Primordial Architects he had dismissed as kindling for his people’s training!
But this entire region was locked down now.
Nothing would be getting in. Nothing would be getting out. Whatever happened here would remain here, and the only witnesses who would leave would be the ones he permitted to leave.
His voice carried calmly across the island.
"You know a lot about me."
His eyes held Octavius’s pale gold ones without wavering.
"But I don’t know too much about you. The circumstances are asymmetric, and I’d like to correct that. So here’s how we’ll do it. You have two options, and I’ll let you choose between them."
He let the pause settle, tyrannical in its patience.

"Option one. You put yourself up on that table. You lie down beside the subject you’ve been working on, and you let me take a look at you. I open you up carefully. I study the engineering that THE Gilded Ones wrote into your existence. I learn what I came here to learn. At the end, depending on how things go, I may or may not let what’s left of you keep breathing."
His gaze drifted briefly toward the fungus-laced corpse at the center of the gathering.

"Option two. You tussle with me first. You and your peers here put up whatever resistance you think you can muster, and we see how far that gets you. And when the tussling is done, I put your corpse on that table to join the one already there. Then I still study you. I still learn what I came to learn. The only difference is that in option two, you don’t get a chance to guide my hands away from anything important, because your hands won’t be moving at all by then."
The island fell quiet around his words.
"Which one...would you like?"
The moment the question landed, Octavius’s smile stretched extremely wide.
And then he began to laugh!

chapters.title: Chapter 5131: Greed! III
paragraphs: The laugh rolling out of Octavius was an ugly one.

It wasn’t the laugh of a being who had lost control. It was measured, scholarly, and almost delighted! He waved his hands upward as if surrendering to a tide he couldn’t turn back, the gesture so disarming it nearly sold itself as sincere.
"Alright, big guy."
His smile held the brilliance of a host welcoming a long-anticipated guest.

"You are far too complex for us little things. Which table would you like my body on so you can take a look? Whichever arrangement suits your research methodology, I’m happy to oblige. I have preferences myself, but I’m willing to be flexible on my preferences today."
Something shifted in the weavings around the island.
|Warning: Civilizational Weaving of Unity has been detected.|
|The weaving is infused into the ambient Infinity and is attempting to propagate along contact vectors. Targets: Noah Osmont. Naldine Manthon. THE Living Emotive.|
|Effect Goal: Infiltrate existential foundations and establish infectious Unity bond with source entity.|
Noah’s eyes sharpened.

That was why Octavius was smiling. The surrender was theater. The welcome was bait! He had already embarked on an attack the moment the words left his mouth, threading his Civilizational weaving through the ambient Infinity that was already saturating the island, using the density of the environment as camouflage for a strike that would have rooted itself into the existences of all three of them before any of them had time to notice.
It wasn’t even a bad attempt!

Against a lesser party, it would have worked. Against Noah alone, it might have given him pause for a fraction of a moment. But the weaving had reached not only for him. It had reached for Naldine too.
His eyes turned unfathomably cold.

It wasn’t the attack itself that did it. What cooled his gaze into something glacial was that the reach had extended toward Naldine, toward the Hadean woman floating beside him whose radiant white hair caught the filtered light of THE Wyld’s strange sky.
Grand and tyrannical and calculating though he was, there were weaknesses he had never bothered to hide from himself.
Women were one of them.
His women, specifically.

Once a bond settled between him and someone he counted as his, he became overly protective in ways that his pragmatic self couldn’t quite discipline out of existence. If there was a single emotion associated with him that could have been amplified into an Ego that made him immune to the madness of Infinity, it probably wasn’t pride.

He wasn’t overly prideful. Rage and wrath came when they came, but they didn’t last long enough. Lust, though. If one wanted to make a case, Lust might have been it! Even though he knew for him and how he played with infinity, emotions shouldn’t be the answer of why he never went mad.
Such a thought crossed his mind in the space between heartbeats.
He shook his head once and focused down on the island.
"Okay," he said calmly. "Second option, it is."
He wanted to test things.

Here were powerful Primordial Architects whose engineered capabilities he couldn’t properly gauge from observation alone. The seas of Infinity inside them told him they were stable. The amplified Egos told him they were designed to resist madness.

But the actual combat ceiling of each being, the exact pressure they could withstand, the point at which their engineered stability began to crack, none of that could be derived from inspection. It required contact.
So he struck with an attack that would have decimated someone like Grimvault.
He stayed where he was. He raised his hand, and with a simple motion he pushed it down through the air.
HUUM!
In the next instant, identical visages of his body appeared in front of each Primordial Architect gathered below.

Each copy held the same posture. Each copy pushed its hand down with the same slow deliberateness. The air between him and every single target collapsed into a Geodesic Weaving of infinity, a sea of infinity, one attack distributed across multiple points simultaneously, one movement propagating through the ambient Infinity until it arrived at every target in the same instant it left him!
Because Infinity was pervasive, his attack became pervasive. One gesture. Infinite vectors!
Oh!
Behind each pushing hand, a concentrated sea of Infinity pressed downward with the full weight of his Hadean physiology riding its current.
BOOM!
The island rocked on its foundations!

Every Primordial Architect below was hammered backward. The Rhyacian Tier scholar at the rear of the cluster was flung across the length of the island before her body even registered being hit. Two Calymmian peers slammed through their own apparatus, flasks shattering around them, bone towers toppling onto their crumpled forms. The research grounds that had stood for eons finished their rearrangement in less than a second.
Two figures remained standing.
Octavius and Valeria held their ground.
They had both been struck. He had seen the impact land on them, had felt the resistance his weavings encountered. But neither of them had been knocked back. Neither of them was even visibly strained!
Valeria’s crimson braids swayed once from the force and settled. Octavius adjusted the cuff of one emerald sleeve with the fingers of the other hand as a faint sea of infinity swirled around him.
|The weight of Infinity and Quintessence Infiniforce distributed equally across all hostile targets.|

|Against all engineered Primordial Architects on the primary island, single-strike termination(one hit, one kill) was not achieved. Engineered stability exceeds standard Primordial Architect thresholds.|
|Result: Five of seven targets incapacitated or displaced. Two targets unhindered.|
|Octavius Kraethos and Valeria Morne have sustained negligible damage.|
Noah’s smile turned dangerous.

"You try sending your infectious weavings of Unity to me or those around me again," he said, his voice drifting across the ruined island with the patience of a decision already finalized, "and I really won’t leave your corpse in one piece."
Octavius smiled brilliantly.
He rolled his shoulders. Cracked his neck once, a small sharp sound that shouldn’t have carried across the distance and somehow did.
"Big guy. Infinity-bearer. Infinite Conduit. Whatever name you want to take for yourself."
His pale gold eyes shone with a hunger that had finally found its proper subject.

"I do wish to tell you that we are not like any Primordial Architects you’ve encountered before. We are the Chosen. Our Egos burn brightly with Greed that radiantly resists the madness of Infinity, the same madness that would have you drowning if you weren’t whatever exception you happen to be. If you thought this was going to be easy, I’m sorry to disappoint. The disappointment...will be educational, I promise."

chapters.title: Chapter 5132: Greed! IV
paragraphs: Octavius tapped one finger against the air beside him.

A unique sea of Infinity bloomed out from his body, this one tinged with the sickly gold-green of Greed refined into fuel. The sea flowed outward and downward, pouring toward the golden table at the center of the island, and the corpse on that table began to tremble.
The fungi laced through its ribs moved.

They wove across the opened chest cavity rapidly, closing the body they had spent so long opening, stitching the subject back together with threads of pale bioluminescence. The corpse’s limbs twitched, then straightened. In a single fluid motion it sat up, then stood, then launched itself off the table to stand before Octavius!
Rivers of Infinity surged down toward it from every direction, the diverted channels of the research apparatus finally feeding into their intended recipient.
Noah observed all of it.

The body that straightened in front of Octavius was unfinished. The engineering was raw. The weavings holding it together strained against each other in configurations that shouldn’t have held at all. And then it opened its eyes.
WO! WO! WO!
Glistening blue crystalline pupils of pure Infinity shone out from a face that had been a corpse a moment earlier.
He understood what he was looking at instantly!
Madness.
THE Gamaidian.

The creature’s eyes held the madness of Infinity the way a lantern held flame, and his own eyes lit up with interest at the sight of it. So this was what Octavius’s latest product looked like when it stood? An abomination made from the collision of flooded Infinity and something else, held together by engineering that shouldn’t have been possible and somehow was!
|Entity Detected: Unnamed Abomination, Latest Product of Octavius Kraethos.|
|Status: Conscious. Hostile. Unstable.|
|Current Scale: THE Proterozoic Scale - Calymmian Tier verging on Ediacaran Tier(Again, Scale ranking is not to be trusted).|
|Engineering Signature: THE Gamaidian saturation paired with unstable amplification of Ego of Hunger. Control tether active and routed through Octavius Kraethos.|
|Threat Level: Unknown. Combat parameters cannot be fully predicted due to unstable modifications.|
Beside him, Emotive moved to speak.
Noah raised his hand and stopped her before the first syllable left her mouth.
"Stand back and do not interfere."
His voice held the quiet steadiness of a directive that didn’t need to be repeated.
"Naldine, keep an eye on the surroundings. Make sure nothing new bothers us while I’m working. I feel like I’ll be getting a bit serious here."
His gaze settled on the abomination with its glistening mad eyes.
"I want to see. I want to see!"
BOOM!
Terrifying pressure erupted out from his standing form.

It rolled outward in every direction at once, invisible to the eye and yet perceivable by every existence within its range. The ambient air buzzed. The floating island trembled beneath him. The diverted rivers of Observable Force shuddered in their courses!
Even Naldine’s existence braced slightly as the wave passed over her, her vihuela humming awake in response to the density of what had just been released.
|Civilization Activation Detected: THE Hadean Haki of Infinity.|

|This authority extends from your Cause and applies existential pressure across the surrounding region. Common Rhyacian and Calymmian Tier Proterozoic Scale entities cannot move freely under the weight of this Haki while your Cause sustains it. Higher-tier entities will experience significant hindrance depending.|
Naldine’s singularity-dotted eyes widened with astonishment.
She had sparred with him. She had been filled by him. She had been present for his ascensions and witnessed the unfolding of each new capability as it bloomed across his Hadean foundation!
And even she looked at him differently now, her frown tightening with the specific respect of a being who had just been reminded that she hadn’t yet mapped the full breadth of what he was.
Emotive turned toward him with eyes that had gone fervent in a way that bordered on religious.
On the island below, the Rhyacian Tier Primordial Architect who had been flung across the surface simply lost consciousness.

Her body went slack where it had been crumpled. Her power sputtered out of her like a candle in a draft, unable to maintain itself against the weight of Haki that her engineering wasn’t ready to process.
The other Primordial Architects who had been flung aside struggled to rise.

Their limbs shook. Their own weavings of authority slowed to sluggish crawls. They could move, barely, but they couldn’t move freely. The pressure had turned their every motion into labor, and their Greed-amplified foundations weren’t optimized for this particular kind of resistance.
Octavius smiled heavily.
He shook his head with the delighted incredulity of someone who had been presented with an even grander puzzle than he had bargained for.
"Man."
He rolled his shoulders beneath the pressure, working himself loose by fractions.
"Are you really the real deal? Man, alright! Come then! You may be grand, I’ll grant you that, you may be something the ordinary methodologies haven’t accounted for. But you..."
His pale gold eyes gleamed brightly through the weight of the Haki.
"You are not a Chosen."
He wasn’t Chosen?
So that was how they framed it internally. Being selected to be engineered by THE Gilded Ones was, in their own scholarly vocabulary, being Chosen. Capital fuckin’ C!
The grand distinction between themselves and every other being across Observable Existence. The mark of having been selected from among the many to receive what the many would never touch.
Hah.
He detested the idea of chosen ones.

Nobody chose anyone to be the savior of everyone. The concept was a convenient fiction that fake chosen ones told themselves to feel grander than the circumstances that had produced them, and it was the same fiction their beneficiaries used to justify whatever hierarchies they had built on top of that designation.

One had to move their own ass! One had to do everything they could with the power they actually possessed. Not because some higher entity had pointed a finger and whispered you. Not because some engineering protocol had written superiority into their foundations before they ever drew their first breath.
You acted because you were capable.
You rose because you refused to stop rising.
Chosen was a word for those who needed permission to matter.
He did not need permission to matter!
Nobody pointed a finger at him and said hey, you are the Chosen One!
Noah lowered his hand slowly, the Haki settling into its sustained state around him, and he looked down at Octavius at this moment, rivers of blue and gold began to seethe around him!
Existence seethed, and battle bloomed explosively!
The abomination moved first.
It launched from its standing position in front of Octavius without a wind-up, without a tell, without any of the telegraphed aggression!

One instant it stood beside its maker. The next instant it was in the air above Noah, its glistening blue crystalline pupils burning with madness locked onto him with the single overriding directive of its amplified Hunger.
Its mouth opened!

It opened wider than its jaw should have allowed, then wider still, the fungal stitching across its chest splitting down the middle to reveal a second mouth beneath the first. Rivers of mad Infinity poured from both openings, saturated with THE Gamaidian, warped into configurations that bit at the edges of perception. The entire sky above Noah became a gullet reaching down to swallow him whole!
Noah stood where he was.
He raised one hand.

Observable Force surged up from the rivers woven through the island, answering his call with the obedience of currents bending toward a moon. It pooled in the palm he had raised, condensed into a disc of golden pressure that weighed the open air down around it, and he pushed.
The disc of Observable Force met the descending gullet at its apex.
BOOM!

The abomination’s two mouths slammed shut against the disc and couldn’t close further. Its jaw stretched against pressure that refused to yield. Its eyes rolled back briefly as the mad Infinity pouring from its openings rebounded down its own throat, and it was thrown upward through its own attack, spinning end over end across the ruined sky of the island!
WU! WU!
Octavius tapped two fingers together.

Weavings of Unity bloomed outward from the motion. Pale tendrils of concentrated weavings of Primordial Mycelia reached through the ambient Infinity like roots through loose soil, seeking every surface they could bond to. They reached for Noah’s feet. They reached for the air around his lungs. They threaded along the island’s stone, trying to establish contact vectors that would let Unity propagate into his existential foundations.
They reached Naldine as well.
They got nowhere near her.

Her vihuela hummed awake behind her, and a single note rang out across the floating island, clean and cold and causal. The Unity weavings that had reached for her unraveled back along their own paths, not destroyed, simply rewritten, so that their original intent became something that had never quite happened. Naldine’s singularity-dotted eyes held Octavius’s pale gold ones with the calm disdain of a Hadean woman who had been briefly interrupted!
The weavings reaching for Noah fared differently.
They touched his Hadean Dermis of Infinite Interface, and they dissolved against it like salt against a sea. The Unity bond couldn’t find a foundation to root into!

His engineering didn’t present the attachment points the Mycelia required. The tendrils flailed blindly across his skin for a fraction of a moment and then simply faded, their reach spent against a surface that refused to acknowledge them.
Valeria moved in from the left at this time as these three swarmed Noah!
HUUM!

Her approach was different from Octavius’s. Where he built, she cut. Her hands carried blades of compressed Infinity that sang as they sliced through the air, each edge honed into configurations that would have severed the weavings of most Calymmian Primordial Architects before those weavings could register being cut. She closed the distance in three strides, and on the third stride her blades were already falling toward his neck!
Noah caught both of them.

His Hadean Hands of Infinite Grasp closed around the edges as if they were wooden dowels, and the Infinity she had poured into her weapons drained down his arms in visible currents, pulled into his own reserves through contact alone!
Oh!
Her dark eyes widened for the first time since she had entered the engagement. Her hands tried to pull her blades back. They didn’t come!
He leaned his head toward her slowly.

"Greed," he said conversationally, his voice pitched for her ears alone. "That’s the Ego they amplified in you. The hunger for what you don’t yet have. You reach for my Infinity, and I thank you for the offering. The weavings... feed better when they’re willingly given."
Her mouth opened to respond.
He released one of her blades and used the freed hand to slap her across the temple with a casual backhand!
WAA!

chapters.title: Chapter 5133: Greed! V
paragraphs: Valeria spun once through the air, hit the stone of the island, skidded, and came up into a crouch twenty paces away. Her braids had come loose along one side. A thin line of golden blood traced down her cheek from the corner of her brow. She straightened with measured calm, her shoulders rolling as she reset her posture, and then she drew both blades of infinity again without a word.
Above, the abomination completed its spin.
It came back down toward Noah faster than it had gone up!
Its jaws didn’t open this time. Its hands extended forward in front of its body, and from those hands erupted long jagged talons made of concentrated madness, THE Gamaidian given edge and purpose!
The air screamed around the talons as they descended, Infinity twisting into configurations that refused to resolve into any stable geometry.
Octavius launched new weavings from behind the abomination.

His Unity reached through the air in coordination with the abomination’s strike, not trying to bond with Noah now but trying to bond with the talons themselves, trying to graft them into Noah’s body once they connected so that the embedded weapons would root and spread and turn Noah into new soil for Primordial Mycelia.
Valeria came in from the left again at the same instant.
Three angles. Three attacks!
Three different methodologies converging on his standing position with the precision of a rehearsal that had been waiting!
Oh!
Noah watched all of it.
His eyes drank in the weavings as they approached. The mad Infinity of the abomination, wild and beautiful in its chaotic saturation. The Unity of Octavius, patient and infinite in its approach!

Valeria’s cutting Infinity, clean and scholarly in its geometry. Three different expressions of what Infinity could become in the hands of beings who had been engineered to hold it, and all three of them reaching for him at once.
He found himself genuinely interested.

The madness especially. THE Gamaidjan was rare. Most beings who fell into it were consumed too quickly for any meaningful study, their weavings dissolving into incoherent pressure before anyone could trace what the madness was actually doing to them at the fundamental level. But here it was, harnessed, walking, attacking with something that passed for strategy!
Octavius had achieved something grand.
Noah smiled brilliantly.
He raised both his hands upward into the descending convergence of attacks.
HUUM!
Seas of blue Infinity erupted outward from his body in concentric waves, the blue deepening throughcobaltand into something closer to void as the density compounded against itself.

Multicolored Quintessence Infiniforce bloomed between the blue currents, golds and violets and purple and silvers braiding through the blue without mixing with it, each color holding its own distinct weaving. The ambient Infinity of the region bent toward him. The rivers of Observable Force on the island curved upward to feed his expanding authority!
Above his head, THE Hadean Pillar of Infinity manifested.

It rose from his crown as if it had always been there and had simply been waiting for permission to be seen. Crystalline blue trees of THE First Tongue formed its base. Multicolored flames of Existence licked through its mid-tiers. Infinite mirrors of Paradox reflected impossibilities at every angle. The eternal storm of Chaos swirled at its apex, and beneath that apex the additional actualized Civilizations layered themselves in concentric halos of authority!
The Pillar towered upward toward a sky that suddenly seemed very small by comparison.
His voice rolled out across the island with calm grand finality.
"Freeze."
HUUM!
Every entity whose body held Infinity within it froze in place!
The abomination’s descending talons halted a hand’s width from Noah’s upraised palms. Its body hung in the air above him, arrested mid-motion, its glistening mad eyes wide and unmoving!

Octavius’s Unity weavings stopped propagating, their tendrils suspended in the act of reaching, their patient weavings paused between one breath and the next. Valeria’s blades froze at the edge of their arc, her dark eyes locked on Noah from her approaching stride, her braids still half-loosed from the earlier impact.
On the broader island, the Primordial Architects who had been struggling to rise stopped rising.

The ones who had been knocked unconscious remained unconscious, their Infinity reservoirs held still within their stalled forms. The ambient rivers of Infinity threading through the island paused in their golden flow, their currents held motionless as if the island’s entire circulatory system had been told to wait!
|Civilization Activation Detected: THE Hadean Pillar of Infinity - Dominion of Internal Infinity.|

|This authority extends from your Pillar into every existence whose body holds Infinity within the surrounding region. You have asserted temporary control over the Infinity inside each affected being.|

|Strain Analysis: Negligible strain against common Proterozoic Scale entities. Minor strain against engineered subjects. Moderate strain against the abomination due to its unstable saturation with THE Gamaidian.|
|Duration: Sustainable for an extended period at current Civilizational Access. Release of authority is at your discretion.|
Only Naldine and Emotive remained moving.
He hadn’t extended the authority toward either of them. Naldine, because she was his. Emotive, and because there was no point in freezing his own tool.
He laughed.

It rolled out of him low at first, a sound that startled the shocked Naldine beside him because she had rarely heard it in this register. It built as he laughed, rising into something louder, something that bordered on the mad but never quite crossed the threshold, because he wasn’t mad!
He...wasn’t mad!

He was delighted. Waves of blue and multicolored Infinity shone across his skin as he laughed, his hair radiating its multicolored light in pulses that matched the rhythm of his amusement, his fair skin illuminating gold from within as if a sun had decided to use his form as its vessel!
"Infinity!"
His voice rolled out between bursts of his laughter.

"All of you, every single one of you, you carry it inside yourselves and you speak of it as if it belongs to you. You call it yours. You cultivate your amplified Egos to withstand it, and you tell yourselves that the withstanding is mastery. That holding the flood makes the flood into something that serves you!"
He laughed again, tilting his head back slightly.
"It never belonged to any of you!"
His Pillar blazed brighter above him.

"Infinity doesn’t have owners. It has channels. Every being who carries a sea of it inside their chest is a channel, and channels do not dictate the direction of what moves through them. You were engineered to hold a flood that was never yours, and the best of you learned to pretend the flood was obedient. The pretense worked because nobody had ever come along to correct it. And now I’m here. Now someone has finally come along!"
"I HAVE COME!"
BOOM!
He spread his arms wider, Pillar towering, Infinity blooming in every direction.
"So hold still."
His smile stretched slowly.
"I’d like to look at each of you properly. Show me your infinity...and I will show you mine!"
WAA!
The island held its breath around him.

Above, the abomination’s frozen eyes still burned with their trapped madness, and Noah turned his gaze toward those eyes first as astoundingly...a bright blue of utter glory and superiority reflected in his eyes!
But he was not mad.
No. He...was not mad!

Moderate strain against the abomination due to its unstable saturation with THE Gamaidian.|
|Duration: Sustainable for an extended period at current Civilizational Access.
Release of authority is at your discretion.|
Only Naldine and Emotive remained moving.
He hadn’t extended the authority toward either of them.
Naldine, because she was his.
Emotive, and because there was no point in freezing his own tool.
He laughed.
It rolled out of him low at first, a sound that startled the shocked Naldine beside him because she had rarely heard it in this register.
It built as he laughed, rising into something louder, something that bordered on the mad but never quite crossed the threshold, because he wasn’t mad!
He...wasn’t mad!
He was delighted.

Waves of blue and multicolored Infinity shone across his skin as he laughed, his hair radiating its multicolored light in pulses that matched the rhythm of his amusement, his fair skin illuminating gold from within as if a sun had decided to use his form as its vessel!
"Infinity!"
His voice rolled out between bursts of his laughter.
"All of you, every single one of you, you carry it inside yourselves and you speak of it as if it belongs to you.
You call it yours.
You cultivate your amplified Egos to withstand it, and you tell yourselves that the withstanding is mastery.
That holding the flood makes the flood into something that serves you!"
He laughed again, tilting his head back slightly.
"It never belonged to any of you!"
His Pillar blazed brighter above him.
"Infinity doesn’t have owners.
It has channels.
Every being who carries a sea of it inside their chest is a channel, and channels do not dictate the direction of what moves through them.
You were engineered to hold a flood that was never yours, and the best of you learned to pretend the flood was obedient.
The pretense worked because nobody had ever come along to correct it.
And now I’m here.
Now someone has finally come along!"
"I HAVE COME!"
BOOM!
He spread his arms wider, Pillar towering, Infinity blooming in every direction.
"So hold still."
His smile stretched slowly.
"I’d like to look at each of you properly.
Show me your infinity...and I will show you mine!"
WAA!
The island held its breath around him.

Above, the abomination’s frozen eyes still burned with their trapped madness, and Noah turned his gaze toward those eyes first as astoundingly...a bright blue of utter glory and superiority reflected in his eyes!
But he was not mad.
No.
He...was not mad!

chapters.title: Chapter 5134: Dissection! I
paragraphs: THE Living Emotive had been siphoning emotions across Observable Existence for a time now. She had been cataloguing the flavors of every feeling she could pull down from the ambient currents. She had been doing this with the calm professionalism of someone who knew her own craft!
And she had never, ever, ever felt an Infinity like her Fixation’s.
Like, really. She wanted to be clear about that.

The ones on this island? Fine. Ordinary flavors. Recognizable. Octavius first, because he was the loudest of them, emotionally speaking. His signature rolled across the ambient air in layers, and her senses peeled every layer apart without effort, and every single layer beneath the surface tasted the same.
Greed. Anh, so much Greed!
Not the petty kind. Not the kind lesser beings carried when they wanted a friend’s wife.

This was Greed refined across eons into a discipline. Greed cultivated into methodology. Greed so precisely engineered that it had become the vessel his Infinity rested inside. His sea of it tasted sharp and hungry and organized, and the organization was the whole trick. The Greed held the flood the way a dam held a river, and the river obeyed because the dam had been designed to be obeyed.

Valeria’s Infinity tasted similar, but sourer. Sheesh, so much sourer! Her Greed carried the tang of someone who had watched three failed experiments before this one and had folded each failure into her own ambition. The Rhyacian one collapsed on the ground tasted duller. Just flat Greed, plateaued, the kind that stopped reaching because its owner had stopped reaching. The other Calymmians between them, all variations on the same chord, different notes in the same engineered song.
The Abomination, though.
Oh!
The Abomination!

Emotive’s hair rippled through colors she usually saved for mourning as she looked at it. The emotion pouring off the frozen creature was a single note held too long. Held so long it had stretched past music into something that ate music!

Hunger. Endless Hunger. But the Hunger was already collapsing into THE Gamaidjan around the edges, and where the two met, something that wasn’t quite an emotion pulsed beneath the surface. It was...Madness.

The madness of Infinity on a leash. The leash was fraying. Mmm, she could see it fraying, and Octavius clearly hadn’t finished tying the final knots before her Fixation had shown up with his questions and his Pillar and his extremely inconvenient timing.
Then she turned her senses toward Noah. Her Fixation!
And every comparison broke.

She wanted to say this carefully, because she was feeling a lot right now and she wanted to be a good little witness to what she was experiencing instead of spiraling, which she could absolutely do if she wasn’t paying attention.
His Infinity...didn’t taste of a single Ego.
It tasted of everything.

Her hair burst through colors she hadn’t known lived inside her palette. Layer upon layer upon layer of emotion, each one distinct, each one stable, each one woven into the next without any of them dominating. Calm sat beside rage, and neither contaminated the other. Tenderness coexisted with tyranny in the same breath, and the tenderness didn’t make the tyranny soft and the tyranny didn’t make the tenderness cruel.

Hunger pulsed alongside satisfaction. Pride breathed next to humility. Cruelty held hands with mercy. None of it was contradictory. None of it was warring. None of it was collapsing the others out of the picture, which, like, emotions normally did that, emotions usually wanted the spotlight, and here they were sharing it!
Was that his secret? Was that it? Was that really it?
Oh!
Was that why he was immune to the madness of Infinity?
She thought about it the way she thought about everything.

The engineered ones amplified a single Ego to hold the flood. Simple solution, elegant even, she could respect it. But her Fixation, THE Youngest, had amplified all of them. Countless colors of emotion, each one as cultivated as Octavius’s Greed, each one as refined as Valeria’s cutting discipline, each one its own channel for his Infinity to rest within. If one Ego could hold a flood, then countless Egos could hold an ocean. And the ocean would move through him without madness, because no single weaving would ever be asked to hold more than it had been built to carry.
Her eyes shone brilliantly as she watched him move like a work of art. And he fucking was a work of art!
Then he raised his hands, and hismassivePillar manifested above him, and he said the word.
"Freeze."
Okay. Okay okay okay!
Her existence trembled with fervor as his Infinity poured outward, and what she saw with her emotional senses...oh, oh, oh!

In the Infinities filled with Greed and Hunger and all the carefully amplified Egos of the engineered, she felt his emotions flourish. His grand weavings threaded into their seas the way ink threaded into water. Spreading along every channel they had cultivated so carefully. Finding the precise emotional foundations their Egos had built. And then just taking them over. Like it was nothing!
Their engineering became the instrument of his authority!
The Greed that had held Octavius’s flood in place now held still, because Noah’s weavings had climbed through Infinity into that Greed and pulled the reins.
He hadn’t broken their engineering.
He had used it.
He had used it!
He had used it, and she was never going to recover from the elegance of that.

Every being whose body held Infinity locked in place, and she felt it happen from the inside, because her senses worked from the inside, and she felt the frozen ones stop moving because something grander had threaded itself through their own reservoirs of infinity and told those reservoirs to still.
Emotive blinked.
She blinked again!

Her Fixation laughed, his voice rolling out across the island, waves of blue and multicolored Infinity shining across his skin, his hair radiating pulses of colors she had never seen on any being’s head. Her heart beat so rapidly that she had to pull on emotions of calm just to hear herself think!
And even then her hair kept flickering between silvers and pure radiant whites!
Was her Fixation not truly mad?
Was he?
Wasn’t he?
Mmm. The thought lodged itself in her for a moment, and she turned it over, because comparison was the only tool she trusted when she was this overwhelmed.

She turned her senses back to the Abomination. The creature’s frozen eyes still burned with THE Gamaidjan. When she tasted that madness, what she found beneath it was emotion that had collapsed into a single unstable note. A single hungry scream. A scream that had lost the ability to be anything except itself. That was madness. That was what madness felt like from the outside. One note, forever, no harmony.
Then she turned her senses back to Noah.
His emotions were far too stable for that.
Far too stable. Far, far too stable. Far, far, far too stable!

Countless colors, every one of them distinct, every one of them content to exist alongside every other. Harmony wasn’t even the right word, because harmony implied a small number of notes in agreement. This was a symphony. And the symphony was so large that the absence of any single note would have made the whole composition noticeably smaller.
Her Fixation couldn’t possibly be mad.
No.
He was not mad.
She shook her head slowly, her hair settling into a deep reverent gold, and she kept watching him laugh with his hands raised and his Pillar blazing above him!

chapters.title: Chapter 5135: Dissection! II
paragraphs: Noah’s eyes were bright as he looked at the bound Primordial Architects floating before him.

Above him, THE Hadean Pillar of Infinity buzzed with the soft hum of a forge just before its next strike. He called upon the Civilizations nested within it, and three of them bloomed outward at his summons. Undifferentiated Fate first, its golden light pouring down from the Pillar in long molten ribbons.

Relativity next, its purple currents folding through the space around him in configurations that bent distance into obedience. Outerversal last, its obsidian weavings rising from the depths of the Pillar like something fished up from a sea that had no bottom.
The three Civilizations wove together in the air in front of him and became chains.
Golden, purple, and obsidian. Braided along their lengths, each link carrying the weight of all three Civilizations at once.

His Pillar of Infinity held every actualized Civilization he possessed.That had been the point of building it this way. He could call on them individually, layer them however he wanted, and each one would still carry the full weight of Infinity because the Pillar was where Infinity and Civilization met.
The chains moved.
HUUM!

They struck outward across the floating island, uncoiling through the frozen air with the steady confidence of predators that had been bred for exactly this kind of work. They wrapped Octavius first. Then Valeria. Then the other Calymmians scattered across the ruined apparatus!

Then the unconscious Rhyacian. Then the Abomination still hanging above, its jaws still arrested mid-bite. Each being was coiled into its own individual harness, lifted from wherever it had been frozen, and laid flat on its back in space.
Relative to him. He floated above them now.
Below him, they floated in a neat row beneath his position, like specimens on trays!

Shock sat in their eyes. Sombreness behind the shock. Every one of them stared up through the weight of his Haki, and every one of them understood something in that moment that they hadn’t quite believed before the chains had settled around their limbs.
The Chosen designation had limits. The limits had just introduced themselves!
Noah checked the strain inside himself.

It was akin to an invisible muscle deep in his mind held every bound Primordial Architect in place, each one a thread his attention was keeping taut. Octavius took the most force, naturally. The Greed-amplified Architect had the most foundation of the lot, and his engineering pushed back against the control of his Infinity with the most sustained resistance. But even he was manageable!
He waved his hand.

Octavius’s bound body slid through the air toward him, golden and purple and obsidian chains dragging it closer until it hovered directly beneath Noah’s floating position. The Architect’s pale gold eyes held up at him with the defiant light of a being whose Greed hadn’t yet conceded anything.
Defiance was useful. Defiance meant the Ego was still active, still humming, still demonstrating the configurations Noah wanted to study.
Beneath Octavius, Infinity surged.

It gathered from the ambient currents of THE Wyld, poured upward from the rivers of the island, and condensed into a radiant blue table of brilliance. The table materialized beneath his floating body with the quiet finality of an operating surface being delivered. Octavius’s back came to rest against its glowing surface. The chains adjusted, flattening him further, binding his arms out to his sides in the universal posture of subjects who were about to become specimens.
Noah looked down at him.
"The human body is made of countless things."
His voice carried calmly across the island, unhurried and conversational.

"Even without mana. Even without any authority or refinement at all. The human body on its own is a marvel, and most humans go their entire short lives without ever realizing what they’re actually walking around in. Ordinary flesh and bone. Ordinary blood. Ordinary everything. And yet the composition of that ordinary body, if you trace it back far enough, tells a history that stretches across the entire life of its universe."
He watched Octavius’s eyes for a flicker of interest as there was none, but he kept going.

"The body’s made mostly of oxygen. About sixty-five percent by mass. Then carbon, about eighteen percent. Hydrogen, around ten. Nitrogen, three. Then calcium, phosphorus, potassium, sulfur, sodium, chlorine, magnesium. Trace amounts of iron, zinc, copper, selenium, iodine, and so on down the line. Every one of those elements has a story. Every one of them had to be made somewhere before it ended up inside a walking human being."
His fingers moved absently in the air as he spoke, conducting his own words with tendrils of infinity.

"Hydrogen and most of the helium came from the early universe itself, formed in the first three minutes after the Big Bang. Everything heavier was forged inside stars. Carbon, oxygen, nitrogen, all cooked up in the cores of stars that lived and died across billions of years. The calcium in bones? Forged in stellar fusion. The iron in blood? Made in massive stars and then scattered across space when those stars exploded as supernovae. The iodine in the thyroid, the selenium, the heavier elements? Those came from neutron star mergers and the deaths of the largest stars."
He paused, almost amused at his own digression.

"If I could say one thing to every manaless human I ever walked past back in time in the old world, I’d tell them they were unfathomably grand. And it...is not because they achieved anything. Not even because they cultivated anything. Simply because...they were made of the stuff of stars. Every atom in their bodies had been inside a star at some point. Their calcium had been forged in stellar fire. Their iron had ridden a supernova across the cosmos. They were walking around carrying the ashes of dead suns in their bones, and most of them died without ever thinking about it."
Octavius’s eyes held steady, defiance still burning behind them.

"Every single body and existence has age. Every single body and existence has history. The body you’re lying on this table with, Octavius, tells everything it can possibly tell about you. What you went through. What modifications were written into you. How you were engineered. How you were born. What you ate across eons, what you absorbed, what passed through you and left traces. If an existence is studied closely enough, all of this can be extracted. All of it."
He leaned forward slightly, the Pillar above him blazing brighter.

"So here’s the question I’ve been turning over. What is a Primordial Architect made of? What is Octavius made of? If I break your components down to their foundational weavings, can I design a Primordial Architect? If I account for all of your ingredients, all of your authorities, all of the engineering the Gilded Ones wrote into your existential makeup, can I design and replicate you entirely from the ground up?"
His smile was mild!
"What do you think?"

chapters.title: Chapter 5136: Dissection! III
paragraphs: Octavius’s eyes burned colder.
The defiant light in them sharpened into something almost glacial, the Greed behind it refusing to give Noah the satisfaction of a verbal response. Noah didn’t need one. The eyes were answer enough!
He got started.

He waved his hand, and on his palm boundless multicolored Infinity converged together. It braided into a sharp point. It elongated into a blade. It settled into his fingers as a scalpel of pure Infinite light. He twirled it once between his fingers, the way a surgeon might test the balance of a new instrument.
He lowered the scalpel to Octavius’s chest.
The tip touched the skin of a supposed fucking Chosen One, and the skin parted.

The Ego of Greed holding his flood of Infinity in place flickered in response to the wound, and Noah watched that flicker with the close attention of one who had just been shown the first useful data point of the session. The skin peeled back along his scalpel’s path. The deeper tissues followed. Engineered weavings came into view, and they were beautiful in their way, architecturally beautiful, the kind of work Noah could respect even while he was disassembling it.
As he cut, seas of Infinity converged around the region.

In the next instant, multiple bodies of his own materialized into being, each one glowing with the soft blue of concentrated Infinity, each one forming above a different bound Primordial Architect along the row of floating blue tables beneath him. Each duplicate held its own multicolored scalpel. Each duplicate lowered its blade to the chest of its assigned specimen at the same moment. Valeria’s body opened beneath one of them. The Abomination’s body opened beneath a third. The entire research archipelago became, in a breath, a landmass running every dissection at once.
Noah kept his primary attention on Octavius and The Abomination.
As his scalpel moved, his mind drifted.
Ubergulden Adelheid.
THE Gilded Ones.

If they were leaning into emotions as the biggest thing to combat the madness of Infinity, and if he was finding the amplified Ego of Greed written all over this engineered Architect, then a pattern was starting to trace itself across the data. He’d been hearing Ego of Pride, Ego of Wrath, Ego of Passion. Now Ego of Greed was in his hands literally. Emotions being amplified deliberately, cultivated as the channels through which Infinity could be held without triggering THE Gamaidjan.
The pattern was familiar.

Seven deadly sins. That was what was lining up in his head. Pride, Greed, Wrath, Lust, Envy, Gluttony, Sloth. Before, they’d been moral categories and warnings. The dark configurations a human life could fall into if it let its Egos run unchecked.

The Gilded Ones had taken those exact configurations and turned them into engineering specifications. The darkest emotional categories inflated into cultivation foundations grand enough to hold floods of Infinity.

And he’d already had these concepts lodged deep inside him for ages. He’d already actualized them within his Pillar. He held all of them at once, every one of them amplified to functional intensity, every one of them sitting alongside every other without conflict.
The next question was whether the Gilded Ones stopped at sins.

Did they do virtues too? Charity, Patience, Kindness, Humility, Temperance, Diligence, Chastity. The counterweights. If the sins made good channels for Infinity, the virtues should have made good channels as well, and any engineering program worth running would have tested both sides of the equation.
Had they? Was there a whole second category of engineered Primordial Architects out there running on amplified Charity, amplified Patience? Would he find one of those next?
And where did Ubergulden Adelheid fit in any of this?

Which amplified Ego had the Gilded Ones wired into her foundation? Which configuration was she running on, underneath the seal, underneath the surface of the being who’d looked at him with calm golden eyes?
He could find out.
He could connect with her through his Quintessence Infiniforce again!
Octavius’s body splayed open further beneath his scalpel.

The chest cavity parted fully. The engineered weavings laid themselves out for his inspection. The Ego of Greed pulsed in visible patterns across his exposed foundations, a gold-green lattice woven into the deeper substrate of his existence, the channels of his Infinity reservoir clearly defined against the darker weavings beneath.
Noah leaned closer as he began to see!
Minutes passed.

Naldine stayed behind him and watched him while monitoring everything in the surroundings, the good girl she was. Her singularity-dotted eyes swept the edges of Emotive’s emotional blockade and her own Hadean Barrier of Infinity at steady intervals, her vihuela humming softly against her back. Nothing was getting in. Nothing was getting out!
She was handling what he’d asked her to handle, and she was handling it without needing further instruction.

Emotive, the tool, had kept her creepy gaze on him completely the entire time. Her hair had cycled through more color combinations than most Civilizations held in their entire lexicon. He could only imagine the craziness going on inside her mind. He wasn’t particularly interested in imagining it closely.
But right now he paused over the opened and dissected bodies of the Primordial Architects, and his eyes shone brilliantly.
THE Gilded Ones were truly grand.
The engineering laid out beneath him was, professionally speaking, extraordinary.

They hadn’t only amplified an Ego. They’d altered the very makeup of existence in Octavius and the others from the ground up. Greed was the foundation, yes, the emotion they’d selected for cultivation. But the amplification wasn’t a single inflated channel. It was a network. Intricate, layered, woven through every stratum of the subject’s Bounded Lifeform existence.

They’d taken an ordinary Bounded Lifeform and designed within it a latticework of Greed so dense and stable that Infinity could pour through those channels without triggering THE Gamaidjan. The Ego had been made extreme enough to overcome the madness. The flood had been given specific, engineered rivers to flow down!
Oh!
That alone would have been grand work. But they hadn’t stopped there.

Layered beneath the Greed network, written into Octavius’s existential foundations with the kind of quiet precision that only hands grander than his own could have managed, were additional modifications. Silent ones.

The kind a subject would never be able to detect within themselves because the modifications had been branded onto the Civilizational Anchor itself, fused into the very Civilization the subject had anchored their Second Scale to.
Those modifications altered the subject’s thoughts.

Nothing as blunt as commands or compulsions. The modifications made Octavius and his peers genuinely believe they were Chosen. It wasn’t something they had chosen to adopt out of pride. It had been written into them before they’d even known what they were, so deeply that by the time any of them could reflect on the belief, reflection could no longer separate the belief from the self. If any of them ever stood before a Gilded One, immense reverence would pour out of them automatically!

They would do everything they were commanded. Their entire existences could be shut down by the ones who engineered them, because a kill-switch had been woven into the same Civilizational Anchor that held their power together.
It was nasty stuff.
Genuinely nasty! Well-designed, efficient, beautiful in its craftsmanship, but nasty in every moral direction the word could point.
Noah looked down at Octavius and the others and shook his head slowly before he waved his hand.
He understood the intricacies well enough now, and he wanted to apply what he’d learned before he moved on from this island.Towards the peak of power, self-identity was critical.
There were no sages of enlightened minds!

Egos had to be amplified. Many beings did this as a last resort against the madness of Infinity, though he didn’t have that issue himself, not the way they did. But that didn’t mean he had nothing to learn here. His own identity, his own Ego, was another avenue of cultivation he hadn’t fully leaned into, and there was still much to grasp.

Because from everything he’d gathered...from Naldine, from THE Beholder, from THE Creature and from the Living Emotive. From the memories he was currently harvesting out of Octavius and the others on their floating tables. Infinity was only part of the equation. The part that was difficult but ultimately accessible to enough beings with enough cultivation.
There was still THE Primordial Source. And nobody he’d met yet knew what it was or how to access it.

He’d take it slow. He was still getting a grasp of Infinity, and Infinity alone was unfathomably vast, the kind of ocean that rewarded patient swimmers and drowned the impatient ones. He’d engineered his own Scales of Existence using Infinity as the foundational substrate, which meant he could do things Vakochev’s preset Scales couldn’t.

His Scales were infinite! He could change them. He could transform them as he went. He could fold new stages into the existing ones or bolt new stages onto the framework entirely, and the framework would accept those additions because it had been designed to.
He’d established THE First Infinite Scale already and three Demarcations inside it. Infinitas Corpus, completed. Infinitas Architectura, in progress. Infinitas Causa, waiting.
He could alter any of these. If Ego turned out to be critical, he’d include it. If something else worthy came up, he’d include that too!

So the plan was simple. Learn all avenues of Infinity. Grasp as much of it as he could. Keep building his Hadean Pillar of Infinity toward Absolute Infinity in Infinitas Architectura, which was the immediate goal, the milestone he was working toward even as the Pillar blazed above him now. It was one way his power was continuing to rise. If amplified self-identity and Ego was another way, he’d delve into that too.
But first.
He waved his hand, and all the dissected bodies of the Primordial Architects floated up before him.

The Abomination drifted up last, still silently roaring behind its sealed jaw, its chest cavity split open alongside many other things, its glistening mad eyes rolling uselessly inside their sockets. Still alive and still frozen by his Infinity holding its sea of THE Gamaidjan in place.
Noah looked at it and smiled grandly.
"I know what you’re made of now."
His voice carried across the floating island with calm certainty.

"So I’m going to break all of you down. I’ll integrate you into a singular being. I’ll amplify that Greed even further than the Gilded Ones bothered to amplify it. And I’ll rewrite the engineering written into your existences so that it answers to me instead of them. Hang in there, all of you. We’ll see just what you’re made of when I put you back together."

chapters.title: Chapter 5137: Midas!
paragraphs: After such words, he motioned toward his Hadean Pillar of Infinity.
HUUM!

Endless blue strings came down from the Pillar, threading through the air like the descending roots of a tree that reached between dimensions. Alongside them, rivers of the Civilization of Greed poured out of the Pillar as well, golden-green currents braiding themselves into the region.

The blue Infinity held the cold of infinite possibility. The gold-green Greed burned warmly against it, the color of amplified appetite, of accumulation refined into methodology. Together they filled the air above the floating island with a texture it had never seen before.
Noah calmly conducted the strings.
They descended onto Octavius first. The Primordial Architect’s pale gold eyes blazed with even more defiance as the blue threads touched his opened body, but what the fuck could he do?

Defiance paired with weakness meant nothing. Defiance was only meaningful when the one defying had the capacity to meaningfully refuse. Octavius had no such capacity right now. The Greed in his engineering burned brightly, but it burned within chains, and the chains answered to Noah.
Noah’s Existential Engineering began its work.

The process moved the way it had moved when he’d transformed his people into Nascent Hadean Lifeforms, but the focus was different here. He wasn’t lifting Octavius. He was disassembling him. His strings of Infinity threaded into the Primordial Architect’s foundations and began extracting the subject’s own Infinity, replacing it with his own as they went. The Ego of Greed lattice was preserved but reoriented. The rivers of his Civilization of Greed poured into Octavius through the same channels the Gilded Ones had engineered, saturating the lattice with Greed of Noah’s cultivation rather than the ambient Greed Octavius had grown with.
The Primordial Architect’s body began to break down into its component particles.

The blue strings pulled the weavings apart along the seams the dissection had already opened, and Octavius came apart the way a well-built instrument came apart when its maker knew exactly where each joint sat. His bones dissolved into streams of refined power. His organs followed. His existential substrate flowed out of him in currents of gold-green light that surged through the air toward a single destination.
The Abomination.
Noah did the same to Valeria. Then to each of the other Primordial Architects bound, one after another, his strings working across the row in steady sequence. A few minutes was all it took!
The engineered lifeforms of the research archipelago broke down into their components, and every component flowed into the Abomination at the end of the row.
Seas of Infinity churned in the air above the Abomination’s floating body!
WU! WU! WU!

Rivers of Greed flowed into it endlessly. An aura began to blaze out of the creature, an aura that exceeded anything the island had witnessed yet, the accumulated Greed-amplification of seven Primordial Architects now concentrated into a single vessel that was being redesigned on the fly.
And even though he hadn’t called on it, Observable Force began to gather and flow toward the Abomination in steady streams.

Noah watched that flow with mild interest. Observable Force was responding to the transformation on its own initiative, drawn to the process by something in the architecture of what was happening, and he could feel why the moment it arrived. The force was stabilizing the transformation. It was pacifying the volatile interactions between the multiple existences being folded into a single new existence, smoothing the seams, keeping THE Gamaidjan from overwhelming the composite as the composite took shape!
His eyes shone brilliantly as he watched it all unfold.

Toward the end, he implemented the final stage of his engineering. The transformation of the new composite into a Nascent Hadean Lifeform. Seas of Quintessence Infiniforce poured out of him. Observable Force joined the flow on its own again. Both of them cascaded into the Abomination from every direction, saturating its newly-composed foundations, writing the Nascent Hadean engineering into the creature’s bones and organs as its existence settled into its new configuration.
Another minute passed.
BOOM!
A pillar of Infinity, Observable Force, and the radiant allure of endless Greed shot upward from the Abomination’s floating form.

Noah waved his hand and his Hadean Pillar of Infinity consumed the light before it could propagate outward, pulling the signature of the transformation into itself so that nothing across the broader Wyld would be attracted by the flare. The light faded and the auras settled. The composite being hung in the air before him, finished, standing on its own against the weight of its own completion.
He looked at what he’d made.
The Abomination was now an obscenely fat humanoid thing. Wide bloated limbs. Rolls of fatty flesh.

Golden rings of pure Greed wrapped around it in orbits along every limb, at its wrists, at its ankles, at its bulging waist, at its thick neck. The rings pulsed slowly with the amplified Ego now running through every channel of its existence. Fleshy blue-gold wings erupted from its back, heavy and muscular, beating slowly against the air in a way that shouldn’t have generated lift and yet somehow kept the bloated body aloft with perfect ease.
Its face did not match its body.
Its face was supremely handsome!

The kind of face sculptors across ten thousand realms would have fought each other for the chance to render in stone. Sharp cheekbones. A jaw that cut light into neat halves. Gem like eyes deep and golden and dripping with Greed so intense it was almost quintessential!
The ferocity of that beautiful face sat perched on the bloated frame like a crown on a hoarded treasure.
Noah looked at it with shining eyes.

Endless rivers of Infinity surged into the composite being from the ambient environment, drawn by the amplified Sin of Greed running through its foundations at intensity that put the original Primordial Architects to shame.The appetite of this new lifeform was, quite literally, enormous.
"Octavius," Noah said calmly. "Are you in there?"
He asked it with shining eyes, genuinely curious to see what the answer would be.
The Abomination looked at him.

Its golden eyes released a blinding beam of raw power as the gaze settled on him, and in the next instant the creature kneeled in mid-air. Its wings folded neatly. Its bloated limbs pressed themselves into the posture of absolute submission. It bellowed, and the bellow carried terrifying pressure that rolled outward across the island like a tidal wave of devotion!

Even Emotive and Naldine, floating well behind him, were pushed further back by the wave. Emotive laughed in delight as she caught herself. Naldine braced calmly with her vihuela and held her position.
Noah looked at the kneeling Abomination with shining eyes.
He raised his hand and patted the creature’s abominable head.
In front of him, the prompts bloomed into his perception.
|Existential Engineering has concluded successfully. Product designated.|
|Entity Designation: Midas of Endless Appetite.|
|Classification: Nascent Hadean Lifeform.|
|Skeletal Structure: 103 bones at Proterozoic classification. 103 bones at Hadean classification. Full Hadean Physiology projected to occur within accelerated timeframe.|
|Organ Systems: 39 organs at Proterozoic classification. 39 organs at Hadean classification. Full Hadean Physiology projected to occur within accelerated timeframe.|

|Current Scale: THE Proterozoic Scale - Ediacaran Tier. Forceful ascension has occurred due to the composite influx of Quintessentially Amplified Ego of THE Sin of Greed, Infinity, and Observable Force integrated into the entity’s foundational Civilization.|

|Foundational Civilization: THE Civilization of Desecration.This Civilization has bloomed as a consequence of the forceful inclusion of multiple prior conflicting Civilizations into a single composite existence.|
|Accelerated Growth Rate: The Amplified Ego of THE Sin of Greed within Midas drives continuous self-expansion, consumption, and cultivation. Standard cultivation timeframes do not apply.|

|Unique Property: Bounded Uncountable Infinity Capacity. Midas is the first entity aside from yourself, among those under your weavings, capable of holding Bounded Uncountable Infinity within his existence.|
|Fealty: Absolute. Midas of Endless Appetite recognizes you as his Master.|
|Declaration from Midas:|

|"Everything I see, I desire. Everything I desire, I consume. Everything I consume, I lay at the feet of my Master. Command me, and I will eat the Civilizations of your enemies until there are no more Civilizations for them to hide beneath."|
OH!
Noah looked at the wonder before him, and his eyes shone with brilliance!
